name: Kuwait
title: Kuwait Ship Thickness Measurement | Tanker & Port UTM
description: Ship thickness measurement in Kuwait: UTM at Shuwaikh and Shuaiba ports, CAP and ESP gauging for crude tankers at the oil terminals, hull and piping scope.
h1: Ship Thickness Measurement at Kuwait's Ports and Oil Terminals
intro: Kuwait combines two very different shipping worlds: the commercial ports of Shuwaikh and Shuaiba, handling containers and general cargo for the country's imports, and the oil terminals at Mina Al Ahmadi, Mina Abdullah and Al-Zour, where crude and product tankers and LNG carriers call. Superintendents with ships here need gauging that respects terminal rules and the northern Gulf's extreme summer heat. We mobilise a team from India to Kuwait and gauge hull structure, tanks and piping at berth, at anchorage or at the Shuwaikh shipyard.

highlights.p: Tankers lifting Kuwaiti crude and products face oil-major vetting, and older ships are often asked for CAP. We gauge cargo tank deckheads, bottoms and ballast tanks to the scope that the charterer or the CAP assessment calls for.

Kuwait has some of the hottest summers of any port region, and the shallow waters of the northern Gulf are warm and saline. Deck coatings, ballast tanks and sea-water piping on ships trading here deteriorate quickly.

The HEISCO shipyard at Shuwaikh Port, with its floating dock and shiplift, repairs offshore support vessels, tugs, dredgers and other smaller tonnage. In-dock gauging there gives access to bottom plating and sea chests on the local fleet.

port.h: Kuwait's Commercial Ports and Oil Terminals
p: The Kuwait Ports Authority runs the commercial ports. Shuwaikh Port, on Kuwait Bay beside Kuwait City, is the main gateway for containers, general cargo, vehicles and food imports, and is home to the HEISCO shipyard. Shuaiba Port, south of the city next to the Shuaiba industrial area, handles containers, bulk and general cargo for industry and construction. Kuwait relies heavily on imports for what it consumes, so a steady stream of container ships, multipurpose ships and bulk carriers calls at both ports through the year.

The oil side is larger. Kuwait Oil Company's export facilities at Mina Al Ahmadi load crude onto tankers, including very large crude carriers at the offshore loading points, while the refineries at Mina Al Ahmadi, Mina Abdullah and Al-Zour ship refined products. Al-Zour also has an LNG import terminal receiving LNG carriers. Kuwait Oil Tanker Company operates the national tanker fleet, and international tankers on spot and time charter make up the rest. Loading calls are short and terminal access is tightly controlled, so tanker gauging in Kuwait is usually done at anchorage before berthing or after the ship leaves the berth, where the operator and the terminal allow it.

What makes Kuwait distinctive for inspection is the environment at the head of the Gulf. Summer air temperatures are among the highest anywhere, the sea in Kuwait Bay and along the coast is shallow, warm and saline, and dust settles on decks and holds moisture overnight. Ships that trade into Kuwait regularly, such as regional tankers, feeders, offshore support vessels and harbour craft, show accelerated coating breakdown on decks and in ballast tanks, wastage in sea-water cooling lines and sea chests from warm, silty water, and corrosion in air pipes and deck fittings. On crude carriers, heat on the deck plating also drives corrosion under the deck in the cargo tanks, where readings on deck longitudinals and deckhead plating need extra attention.

facilities.h: Where Gauging Is Done in Kuwait
p: At Shuwaikh and Shuaiba, gauging is done alongside during cargo operations, with access arranged through the agent and the port's security. Container and general cargo calls allow deck, hatch, accessible tank and piping work; bulk carriers discharging over several days allow holds to be gauged as they empty. The HEISCO shipyard at Shuwaikh docks smaller ships on its floating dock and shiplift and repairs others afloat at its jetties, which makes it the place for in-dock gauging on offshore support vessels, tugs, landing craft and dredgers working in Kuwaiti waters.

For tankers, the anchorages off the oil terminals are the realistic workplace. Terminal rules at Mina Al Ahmadi and the other oil ports restrict work on board during loading, and gas-free cargo tanks are rare on a tanker arriving to load. Ballast tanks, deck structure, deck piping and void spaces can be gauged at anchor, and cargo-tank work is planned for a tank-cleaning or docking period. Large tankers from Kuwait generally dock in Bahrain, the UAE or further afield, and gauging in Kuwait can provide the first measured view of the ship before that docking.
list: Shuwaikh Port — deck, hatch cover, hold and piping gauging on container, general cargo and ro-ro ships during cargo operations
Shuaiba Port — hold, tank top and hopper gauging on bulk carriers discharging industrial and construction cargo
HEISCO shipyard, Shuwaikh — in-dock hull, sea chest and tank gauging on offshore support vessels, tugs, landing craft and dredgers
Mina Al Ahmadi anchorage — ballast tank, deck structure and deck piping gauging on crude tankers before or after loading, with terminal agreement
Al-Zour — hull, ballast tank and deck piping gauging on LNG carriers and product tankers, planned around terminal rules and the ship's stay
Kuwait Bay anchorages — pre-purchase and condition gauging on ships waiting for berths at the commercial ports

context.h: Port State Control, Vetting and Fuel Rules in Kuwait
p: Kuwait is a member of the Riyadh MoU, and port state control at its ports follows that regime's inspection practice. For tankers, though, the stricter examination usually comes from vetting: oil majors and terminal operators inspect tankers before accepting them, and older crude carriers face questions about structural condition that only measured data can answer. CAP, run by each class society as a voluntary condition rating, is commonly requested for tankers over about 15 years old, and its gauging scope covers cargo tank structure as well as ballast spaces.

The northern Gulf lies outside any emission control area, and the global 0.50% sulphur limit applies. Many of the crude carriers loading in Kuwait run scrubbers, and their wash-water and overboard piping is an established gauging item. Kuwait's national fleet, regional owners and international tanker operators all trade here, and the ships that call most often gain most from tracking corrosion over time. For ESP tankers, thickness measurement in Kuwait before the third renewal survey, or any later one, can show the owner the likely extent of steel renewal before the ship reaches the yard and the off-hire period is fixed.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Kuwait
jobs.p: Ship inspection in Kuwait splits between the commercial ports, where cargo calls set the window, and the oil terminals, where terminal rules push most work to anchorage. Tankers dominate the requests that matter commercially, because vetting and CAP decide whether a ship gets its next cargo. On the commercial side, the requests are more often about docking plans and condition records for regional ships.
list: A crude tanker over 15 years old at the Mina Al Ahmadi anchorage: ballast tank and deck longitudinal gauging to prepare for a CAP assessment requested by a charterer
A product tanker waiting off Mina Abdullah: deck cargo lines and ballast tank boundaries gauged before loading, ahead of an oil-major vetting inspection
An offshore support vessel on HEISCO's floating dock at Shuwaikh: bottom plating, sea chests and double-bottom tanks gauged for its renewal docking
A bulk carrier discharging at Shuaiba: hold frames, hopper plating and tank top gauged hold by hold as the cargo comes out
An LNG carrier at anchorage off Al-Zour: hull and ballast tank gauging agreed with the terminal and the operator, to give a pre-docking steel estimate

logistics: Kuwait International Airport has direct flights from several Indian cities, and the commercial ports and oil terminals are all reached by road from Kuwait City. Shuwaikh and Shuaiba need port passes arranged by the ship's agent through the Kuwait Ports Authority; the oil terminals add their own security and safety induction, and anchorage work needs a launch booked by the agent. Indian technicians travel on Kuwaiti business visit visas, which we apply for once the ship's dates are firm. For any work at or off an oil terminal, we confirm access in writing before the team travels.

faqs.q: Can you gauge a tanker at the Mina Al Ahmadi terminal during loading?
faqs.a: Generally not during loading itself. Terminal safety rules limit work on board, and the cargo tanks of a tanker arriving to load are inerted rather than gas-free. We gauge ballast tanks, deck structure and deck piping at anchorage before or after the loading call, with the terminal's and the operator's agreement, and plan cargo-tank readings for a tank-cleaning period or a docking.

faqs.q: Is CAP gauging something you can help prepare for in Kuwait?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners of older crude and product tankers trading out of Kuwait often need CAP to keep vetting acceptance. We can gauge ballast tanks, deck and accessible structure in Kuwait to show the owner where the ship stands, so that the CAP survey and any steel renewal can be planned before the charterer's deadline rather than after it.

faqs.q: Does the summer heat in Kuwait affect when you can work?
faqs.a: Yes. Kuwait restricts outdoor work in the middle of the day during summer, and exposed steel decks get too hot for reliable readings and safe handling in any case. We take deck and shell readings early and late in the day and use the hottest hours for work inside tanks and enclosed spaces, which keeps the job moving within the rules.

faqs.q: Can you work on ships at the HEISCO shipyard in Shuwaikh?
faqs.a: Yes, where the owner books us for the ship and the yard grants access. HEISCO docks and repairs offshore support vessels, tugs, landing craft, dredgers and similar ships, and in-dock gauging there covers bottom plating, sea chests and double-bottom tanks. We work under the yard's permit system and coordinate with the class surveyor's attendance, so the readings are ready when the surveyor needs them.
